title: Onprem day docket — tech notes & blockers
content:
Quick header: day docket for on-prem at Acorn Health Systems (week 2 of install). Notes are messy — for my eyes and for handoff to SEs.

2024-11-07 08:15 — morning prep
- Pack: laptop + jumpbox USB key + site creds (ok). Confirmed KMS token expired yesterday (customer rotated keys). Need updated KMS role mapping after lunch.
- Environment: 4 hosts (bare-metal), Ubuntu 22.04, kernel 5.15.x, containerd 1.6.8. GPUs: 2x A40 per host. NV driver reported: 525.85.12.

Preflight quick checklist (things I re-check on arrival):
- Network: internal VLANs, no internet egress from server network — must ensure package pre-caching and offline registry mirror.
- DNS: customer uses internal DNS; nodes resolved to short names only. Add /etc/hosts fallback for jumpbox.
- Firewall: iptables + hardware ACLs at top-of-rack. Opened ports: 22 (jump), 443 (control), 8443 (grpc), 10250 (kubelet). Confirmed with NetOps earlier.
- Time sync: NTP behind corporate time proxy — sync OK but drift of ~3s on host-03. Keep an eye.

Notes from the node-level troubleshooting (host-02):
- Symptom: redwood-agent.service repeatedly crash-looping after containerd upgrade on host-02.
  - journalctl -u redwood-agent.service shows socket: "failed to bind: address already in use" for 127.0.0.1:12001. Looks like leftover process from previous install (legacy sidecar) still listening.
  - ps aux | grep 12001 -> found legacy-proxy process (customer app). Short-term workaround: remap agent to 12002 via /etc/redwood/agent.conf and systemctl restart. Need to file follow-up: coordinated port reassign with customer app owners.

GPU/driver quirks
- nvidia-smi shows MIG unsupported on A40s here (expected). Driver 525 seems compatible with our cuda build but our container image expects nv_peer_mem kernel module for RDMA (InfiniBand). Module not loaded; modprobe nv_peer_mem fails with "not found".
  - Check: vendor did not install Mellanox driver stack. Customer confirmed they only planned RDMA on host-01. For now disable RDMA-backed data plane; use TCP for KV cache replication. Update config: replication.transport=tcp in redwood.conf.

Private network routing gotcha
- Customer's VPC-on-prem gateway translates internal CIDR 10.10.0.0/16 to 172.31.x.y for external services. The sidecar health-checks use the translated address which is not routable inside the cluster. Patch: force health probes to use cluster IPs (Kubernetes Service) rather than external DNS. Add note to runbook.

Security & certs
- Cert rotation: customer uses internal PKI. When we deployed control-plane certs last week we set expiry to 1y by mistake. Ops wants 90d. Need to rotate and coordinate downtime window (small) for control-plane rolling cert update. Jot: schedule after acceptance tests pass.

Recent changes we pushed
- Installer: added offline bundle support, flag --offline-registry=path. Tested locally; at customer site the registry mirror path had an extra subdir causing 404s. Fix: fallback lookup in code. Open PR: github.com/redwood/installer/pull/418.

Open blockers (urgent)
1) KMS role mapping mismatch — blocked creating service account secrets. Impact: cannot pull encrypted model artifacts from S3-compatible store. Next step: meet with customer security 11/09 10:00. Owner: Maya.
2) Port conflict on host-02 (legacy-proxy) — temporary remap done, needs permanent solution. Owner: Arjun to coordinate by EOD.
3) RDMA driver missing for net acceleration — blocks high-throughput KV cache replication tests. Customer to confirm procurement/installation timeline.

Field TODOs (ordered)
- [ ] Push hotfix for installer fallback lookup (PR ref above).
- [x] Remap agent port to 12002 on host-02 (temporary).
- [ ] Add DNS /etc/hosts entries to jumpbox for short names used in playbooks.
- [ ] Update runbook section: health-probe binding to cluster IPs vs external.
- [ ] Re-run e2e latency tests after switching replication to TCP (impact expected ~+3ms).
- [ ] Rotate control-plane certs to 90d (coordinate with ops).
- [ ] Document GPU driver + kernel combo supported matrix in this customer folder.

Hand-off notes for Lucy (tomorrow 09:00):
- Sequence to resume: fix KMS mapping -> verify secret fetch -> re-run model pull tests -> enable caching replication -> run perf harness.
- Logs to check: /var/log/redwood/agent.log, journalctl -u containerd, dmesg for GPU errors.
- Useful commands:
  - sudo journalctl -u redwood-agent.service -f
  - sudo systemctl status containerd && sudo journalctl -u containerd -n 200
  - sudo nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,driver_version,compute_capability --format=csv
  - curl -v --resolve registry.acorn.internal:5000:10.10.1.5 https://registry.acorn.internal:5000/v2/_catalog

Random field notes / ideas while waiting for NetOps response:
- Could we add an installer flag --skip-rdma-check to let teams opt into TCP-only replication? Saves time when InfiniBand not present. TODO: small PR on installer.
- Consider a lightweight agent mode for air-gapped installs: minimal disk footprint, no RDMA, no model cache — useful for initial smoke tests. Label: "agent-lite".

Wrap-up 2024-11-07 18:10
- Made progress but still blocked on KMS and driver pieces. Customer happy with progress and liked the offline bundle idea. Leave this doc as the running journal for next SE rotation.

Notes to self: keep entries terse; include command outputs only when useful; timestamp each day.
